statement: My four contexts use small aggregates with one clear job each: a Person and a Credential prove who someone is; PersonGrants, ChannelAccess and PrivilegeChange decide what they may do; SecretVault and SecretEgress hold and use secrets without their values ever reaching an event; TrustStore and WorkspacePins decide which code may run. The rule throughout is grant slowly, revoke quickly: anything that widens privilege goes through a PrivilegeChange proposal approved by a second person, while every narrowing (revoking, deactivating, rotating) takes effect at once and fans out through policies into the other contexts.

event_changes.why: An unanswered proposal must expire (default 7 days). Otherwise a stale approval could later apply to a target that has changed since; the proposal records the expected version, and expiry closes it.

cloud.eyg defines the workspaces and every named shell, but no event records its versions. ShellDefinitionPublished needs a source CID and author to point back to, just as WorkspaceSourceChanged does for workspace.eyg.

hotspot_resolutions.resolution: Four eyes (approval by a second person) is required for every change that widens privilege or exposure: AdminGranted; PersonShellAssigned to a shell that is not a subset of the current one (same effect fields with identical gate CIDs counts as a subset, anything else counts as widening); an invitation with a non-default shell; any WorkspaceSourceChanged or CloudSourceChanged that adds an effect field to a shell, changes a gate for configuration-API, secret, admin, bind or delegate effects, or changes a secret's allowed hosts; TrustSignatory; IssueApiCredential with an admin-level shell; UnauthenticatedConnectionCreated; and, on Avery's side, retention shortening, legal hold release and erasure. Narrowing never needs approval: revoking, deactivating, AdminRevoked (blocked only if it would remove the last admin), SignatoryRevoked, SecretRotated and channel shells losing fields. SetSecret and RotateSecret by an admin person need one person, because they change a value, not who may use it (hosts live in configuration). An agent can never approve. ApprovePrivilegeChange needs the acting principal itself to be a person (not merely a person at the root of the on-behalf-of chain), using an interactive web shell session signed in within 15 minutes, not an API credential, trigger, schedule or subagent. The approver must differ from the proposer and from the person an agent proposed for. Agents may propose (via the configuration API effects, which become ProposePrivilegeChange when the shell gate allows them), so 'agents propose, people decide' holds. Sole-admin cloud: the only admin may approve their own proposal after a 24 hour cooling-off delay. The approval event is marked self_approved, and the admins view shows a warning until a second admin exists.

Replace the hash placeholder with an opaque random handle created in the vault for each secret version: 'eyg-secret-' plus 128 random bits, mapped to (workspace, name, version) and never derived from the value. Env answers it with a Mock, and the journal records the secret name and version, not the handle, so replay asks the vault for the version's handle. The value fingerprint in SecretSet is an HMAC with a workspace key held in the KMS, so it cannot be checked by guessing offline. Injection becomes explicit only: the egress replaces a handle found in the URL path, query or headers of a Fetch to an allowed host, and records SecretInjectedIntoRequest with name, version, host and step. The implicit 'authorization: Bearer <value>' when no placeholder is used is removed. To migrate, secrets.load takes an explicit 'bearer: True' option per secret, deprecated, and each implicit injection is recorded with mode 'implicit' so the inventory shows which secrets still rely on it. A handle sent to a host that is not allowed causes SecretInjectionRefused and fails the step (it used to pass silently with only a hash leaked). The Redactor scans for both values and handles.

Access view: reading a channel's history is a capability like any other. Grant it through the channel's membership on its platform (mirrored by the chat connection), or explicitly through access for bound people. Admins are not readers by default: an admin reading a channel they are not a member of is a break-glass read, recorded with a reason. Agents read only the history of their own channel; a founders agent reading other channels needs that capability in its shell, approved under O3.
